---
title: "Syllabus & Reading Map"
subtitle: "Mathematical Foundations for AI · 3-1-0-4 · 26 lectures + 13 tutorials, 80 min each"
---

> **Backbone text:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (MML) — [free PDF](https://mml-book.github.io/). Supplemented by Boyd & Vandenberghe (optimization), MacKay (information theory), Solomon (numerics) — all free PDFs.

**Prerequisites:** ES 113 (Data Centric Computing) and ES 114 (Probability, Statistics & Data Visualisation). We assume Python/NumPy and basic discrete probability. We do **not** assume any machine learning.

**Assessment** (advertised structure; dates on the announcements page): quizzes at module boundaries (best n−1) · midsem after Module 3 · endsem (cumulative) · 3 take-home assignments (micrograd · CVXPY · compressor + language model). Tutorials are formative.

## Learning outcomes (from the approved proposal)

Students gain the mathematical tooling for subsequent CS/AI courses, with a mix of theory and programming: numerical representation, linear algebra, multivariate calculus and automatic differentiation, probabilistic modeling and estimation, continuous and constrained optimization, information-theoretic foundations, and sequential models.
